claims.text: Overall survey adherence among patients with major depressive disorder using the Mindful Moods personal smartphone app was 77.78% over a 30-day period.
Survey completion rates varied significantly across times of day, reaching 84.2% in the afternoon compared to 75.5% in both the morning and evening.
PHQ-9 score estimates calculated from app responses strongly correlated with paper-administered PHQ-9 scores (r = 0.84).
PHQ-9 scores obtained via the smartphone app were on average 3.02 points higher than paper-based PHQ-9 scores.
Nine out of 13 subjects (69%) reported significant suicidal ideation via the app, whereas zero subjects reported significant suicidal ideation on the paper-based PHQ-9.
App survey completion rates stabilized after approximately two weeks of study participation.

evidence.description: A total of 903 of the 1161 short surveys administered to the cohort were completed, yielding an overall adherence of 77.78%.

The percentages of surveys completed were 75.5% (292/387) in the morning, 84.2% (326/387) in the afternoon, and 75.5% (292/387) in the evening. Analysis of variance showed a statistically significant difference in these adherence rates.
The two scores were fairly strongly correlated, yielding a Pearson correlation coefficient of .84 (95% CI .55-.95).
We found that the app scores were on average 3.02 (SD 2.25) points higher than paper scores.
while no patient reported suicidality at a level of 2 or 3 on the paper-based PHQ-9, a total of 9 of the 13 subjects (69%) reported suicidal ideation on the app at these levels.
adherence appeared to increase after a few days, decrease, and ultimately stabilize after about 2 weeks.

methodologies.name: Mindful Moods Personal Smartphone EMA
methodologies.description: An ecological momentary assessment methodology where patients complete up to three daily randomized 3-question PHQ-9 sub-surveys on their personal iOS or Android smartphone over 29-30 days.
conditions: Financial compensation of $50 contingent on >=70% survey completion

methodologies.name: PHQ-9 Daily Score Statistical Estimation
methodologies.description: A statistical estimation technique predicting daily PHQ-9 total scores by combining a 2-week moving average response per item with daily observed score deviations to adjust for question sampling and missing data.
conditions: Random sampling without replacement of 3 PHQ-9 questions per session

limitations.text: Paper-and-pencil ecological momentary assessment is labor-intensive, intrusive, and prone to retrospective data backfilling by patients.
Static clinical rating scales administered at fixed time points are subject to patient retrospective recall bias.
The study sample size was small, consisting of only 13 enrolled outpatients with major depressive disorder.
Subjects received $50 compensation contingent upon completing at least 70% of survey sessions, which may have influenced study adherence rates.
The study lacked a control group to isolate app-based self-reporting from clinical interaction effects.
Subjects knew their app responses were not actively monitored in real time, unlike paper scale responses which received immediate clinical attention.

future_work.text: Evaluating smartphone and related technology apps for the real-time detection and potential prevention of suicidal ideation and behavior.
Developing more sophisticated statistical approaches for predicting composite scale scores from randomized, incomplete smartphone EMA survey data.
Understanding clinical applications and validating clinical correlations of passive data collected from smartphone sensors.
